name: Nha Trang Beach
kicker: The city sand along Trần Phú
summary: The city sand runs along Trần Phú. Vietnam Tourism calls this stretch seven kilometres. A beach ticket was not printed, and neither were swim hours, so both are check on arrival. The national pages put the drier months in January to August. After dark the same shore is the walk, and the night market sits behind 46 Trần Phú.
getThere: You are on Trần Phú. From the airport, minutes were not printed.
heroCaption: The city sand, the wash, and the towers along Trần Phú

notice.title: A beach ticket was not printed
notice.body: Do not treat this shore as free. No page used here prints a beach fee or a swim clock. Check both on the sand.

body: This is the beach the city is for. Vietnam Tourism’s place page treats Nha Trang Beach as the day on the sand, and the seven-reasons page calls Trần Phú a seven-kilometre beach. Hotels face that shore. The evening walk is the same sand, not a second beach.

The dry season on both the national tourism page and the bureau bay page is January to August, and the rainy season is September to December. The bureau prints an average of 26°C. A rescuer’s duty clock was not printed. Chair hire was not printed.
The night market is not on the towel. It is the 137 m walking street behind the cultural centre at 46 Trần Phú, in Lộc Thọ. The provincial page says entry is free and prints no closing hour.

figures.caption: Swimmers in the wash, from the same photograph as the long shore
figures.alt: People standing in the shallow water on Nha Trang’s city beach

gettingThere: The sand is Trần Phú. From a hotel on that road you walk out. From Cam Ranh, the AIP says 27 km from the centre, the city lying to the north, and Vietnam Tourism says about 30 km south. Neither page prints the minutes. Shuttles, taxis, and ride-hailing are the modes Vietnam Tourism names.
